mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 since the previous month is associated with stronger labor market momentum, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite the monthly PAYEMS increase ≥2,000.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% over the prior quarter, it signals stronger aggregate demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% over the prior quarter
failure_condition: GDPC1 - INDPRO ≤ 5% in all relevant quarters, or 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% followed by a rebound in the next month (double-bottom pattern) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as supply constraints ease.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops ≥8% in month t, then rises in month t+1
failure_condition: No clear double-bottom pattern in INDPRO over the 20-day horizon or 20-day returns remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months, the expectation of lower future inflation reduces risk premia, resulting in a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: UNRATE does not fall below 3% for two months or 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST (housing starts) of at least 10% above the prior month's level is a leading indicator of construction recovery and supports positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% from prior month
failure_condition: HOUST does not rise by ≥10% or 20-day returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly rises in GDPC1 and RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 4% each are interpreted as dual demand signals, predicting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up ≥4% AND RSAFS up ≥4% in the same month
failure_condition: Neither GDPC1 nor RSAFS rises by ≥4% or 60-day returns are not statistically positive.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE exceeds 4% for three consecutive months, the expectation of tighter labor markets increases cost pressures, which can lead to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE never exceeds 4% in the relevant window or 20-day returns are not negative.
